task.title: Inspect finite recurrence inventory read-only
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/865 by listing authoritative finite recurrence definitions deterministically without creating or mutating storage.
acceptance_criteria: Open only existing recurrence storage read-only and return valid definitions in exact identifier order.
Ignore unrelated stream namespaces while failing closed on malformed recurrence stream identifiers, events, values, and histories.
Share strict exact projection and grant no clock, occurrence lifecycle, catch-up, dispatch, retry, or execution authority.

attempts.diagnostic: The recurrence integration test failed because open_read_only, list, and InvalidStreamId did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added tests for deterministic listing, non-creation, unrelated streams, invalid identifiers, malformed histories, and read-only enforcement.

attempts.diagnostic: Operators needed discovery without giving the read path write authority or weakening exact recurrence replay.
attempts.patch: Added read-only store opening, exact recurrence stream discovery and ordering, shared projection, typed invalid-stream evidence, and ADR-0040.

attempts.summary: Removed a corruption-triggered panic during review.
attempts.diagnostic: CodeRabbit found database-decoded zero intervals, zero counts, or overflowing final occurrences could reach expect-based assumptions during inventory projection.
attempts.patch: Mapped invalid decoded definitions to InvalidHistory, added direct-SQL corruption tests, resolved the thread, and merged after CodeRabbit's recent-review summary covered 5ade67d1 through exact head a86234f3 with no actionable comments.

outcome.summary: Vela can discover valid finite recurrence definitions in deterministic order through a strictly read-only, fail-closed inventory boundary.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- record validate corpus/development/0166-read-only-recurrence-inventory.json # result: valid development record
nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- corpus inspect corpus/development # result: inspected 171 records: 171 valid, 0 invalid

lessons: Read-only discovery must not create a missing database as a side effect.
Validate every database-decoded invariant before constructing trusted recurrence values.

CodeRabbit found an expect-based panic risk for corrupted zero intervals, zero counts, and overflowing final occurrences; invalid decoded definitions now map to InvalidHistory with direct-SQL regression coverage.
Unrelated namespaces should not block recurrence inventory, but malformed owning streams must fail closed.
An acknowledged fix thread is not a substitute for substantive exact-head incremental review.
